newsitem.title: USA: Two members of Naughty By Nature rap group on bail.
newsitem.headline: Two members of Naughty By Nature rap group on bail.

text.p: Two members of the popular rap group Naughty By Nature, who are accused of possessing guns, were released from a New York jail on Friday after posting $1,000 bail each.

Anthony "Treach" Criss, the trio's lead singer, and Vincent Brown were arrested late on Thursday. Police said the two men, both 26, were stopped separately for driving recklessly in their $60,000 Lexus Cruisers.
A New York criminal court judge ordered the men back to court for a hearing on July 16. They were also told to surrender their passports.
Grammy award winners Brown and Criss signed autographs for court officers and police as they waited for the case to be heard.
Prosecutors said police searched their cars and found loaded 9mm pistols.
Criss was charged with wearing a bulletproof vest. New York state law bars people who are not law enforcement officers from wearing bulletproof vests, officials said.
Lawyers for the rappers said both men had carried guns for several months as protection because of the recent murder of such rap stars as Tupac Shakur and the Notorious B.I.G.
"Their lives have been threatened. They've gotten death threats, verbally, orally and in writing," said Paul Bergrin, Criss's lawyer.

Daniel Ollen, the lawyer for Brown, said his client had just settled a $10,000 unlawful imprisonment lawsuit against New York after plainclothes officers allegedly stopped him and stuck a gun in his face.
Brown's lawyer said the rap group were leaving for Arizona on Saturday to begin a nationwide tour.
Naughty By Nature's best-selling album is Tommy Boy Records' "19Naughty3," with the hit single "Hip Hop Hooray."
